tonight.headline: Pickens joins the report with a shoulder — and he plays Monday
body: Bad news first: George Pickens was limited Thursday with a shoulder, his first appearance on Dallas's report this season (The Big Lead, SI 22 Oct). Dallas play Monday night, and every player on this bench has kicked off by Sunday 18:20 — so if Pickens is going to sit, the call has to be made on Saturday's report. Rashee Rice missed practice again (Chiefs.com).

Better: Jordan Love was full in pads and Matthew Golden practised; LaFleur says there is no concern about Golden's or Watson's status (Yahoo 22 Oct). Josh Jacobs practised in pads; LaFleur is 'ramping him up' and will decide after Friday and Saturday. ESPN now has you 49%, 122.8 to 123.9: Furia Regia swapped Addison in for the season-ending McLaurin at 17:29Z — and Jefferson, full on Thursday, still sits on their bench.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Furia Regia start Jefferson (18.6) over Addison (10.9), Pickens sits Monday without a swap, and the flex scores zero — about a 20-point swing on a 1-point projection.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Saturday's Cowboys report gives Pickens no designation — then the flex is settled and the only open decision is Jacobs over Gordon.

whatWentWrong.title: The lineup tool's contingencies fire too late — twice this week
whatWentWrong.lead: Jacobs's check (Sun 12:55) comes after Gordon's 11:00 kickoff; Pickens's (Mon 16:45) hands the slot to Rice at 0.0.

case.label: What happened
case.body: lineup_check.py times every contingency from the questionable player's own kickoff. For Jacobs the fallback (Gordon) has already started; for Pickens, a Monday-night player, every bench body has played by Sunday 18:20 and its printed fallback is the injured Rice.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Both decisions move earlier: Jacobs only on a clear status by Sunday 10:30, Pickens on Saturday's report (the two cards above). Golden's contingency is fine — Worthy plays after Green Bay's inactives.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: ESPN's lock in this league is per-slot rather than per-player — it is not; a started player cannot be benched.

whatWentWrong.sources: lineup_check.py output · ESPN league file kickoffs

whatWentWrong.title: Week 6 was won with 9.9 left on the bench

case.label: The numbers
case.body: 150.8 to 88.62 over Los Cachanillas; best possible 160.7 (week-6 archive, recomputed this run).

case.label: The lesson
case.body: Both were projection calls that lost — no override, nothing to fix but to keep starting by projection, which is why Rice's card waits on practice rather than on a hunch.

case.body: A projection-set Week 7 lineup leaves more than 15 points on the bench (archive).

waiverAnalysis.summary: The tool's weakest movable receiver is now Rashee Rice (DNP again) — on the screen's exposure list, so not a drop — and three more risers clear that lowered bar. All are vacancy or volume roles and priority never resets. Six weeks of data, still thin. Kupp and Shaheed also printed: Kupp is not in the league file's wire (the validator rejects his id) and Shaheed had no dated reporting — both are covered in the report, not here.
